question:
Using properties of determinants, show that
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1+a & 1 & 1\\1 & 1+b & 1\\1 & 1 & 1+c\end{vmatrix}=ab+bc+ca+abc$$
Hence, find the value of $D$ when $a=2$, $b=-1$, and $c=3$.
explanation:
Transformation of the determinant
Apply $R_1\to R_1-R_3$ and $R_2\to R_2-R_3$:
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}a & 0 & -c\\0 & b & -c\\1 & 1 & 1+c\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=a\begin{vmatrix}b & -c\\1 & 1+c\end{vmatrix}+(-c)\begin{vmatrix}0 & b\\1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=a\left[b(1+c)+c\right]+(-c)(-b)$$
$$D=ab+abc+ac+bc$$
Therefore,
$$D=ab+bc+ca+abc$$

Evaluation
For $a=2$, $b=-1$, and $c=3$,
$$D=(2)(-1)+(-1)(3)+(3)(2)+(2)(-1)(3)$$
$$D=-2-3+6-6=-5$$
Hence, $D=-5$.
